title: [Chapitre] II. Réalisations topologiques des réseaux : notes manuscrites (06/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the last page of the notes. It is a three-line continuation that completes the definition begun on p.17.

Setting from p.17. X is a space, probably a surface or a reasonable topological space. A 'structure de maille' (mesh structure) on X is a pair (A, β). Here A is a closed subset, the 'support' or 'lien', possibly but not necessarily a point. β = {ρ, ρ'} is a 'diviseur': a choice of two 'rives' (banks) along A. Concretely, cutting X along A gives a space X̄^{(A,β)}. It is a topological 'recollement' whose boundary over A consists of two copies A_ρ and A_ρ' (the two banks), and gluing them back recovers X. In the picture A is a cut across an annulus. Orienting the mesh means ordering the banks (ρ before ρ'), i.e. choosing one of the two banks forming the border.

The definition of compatibility of two mesh structures (A_1, β_1) and (A_2, β_2) has three parts:
- (a) A_1 ∩ A_2 = ∅, so that A_2 identifies with a subset of the cut space X̄^{(A_1,β_1)} away from the banks of A_1.
- (b) A_2 is again a 'lien' (a cut locus) in that cut space.
- (c) Let U, V be the two connected components obtained by removing the relevant pieces, built from the banks of A_1 and from A_2 (the notation on p.17 is garbled).

This page finishes (c): 'alors {U,V} se définit à la fois [par] β_1 et β_2'. That is, the bipartition {U, V} into two sides is determined simultaneously by the bank-pair β_1 and by the bank-pair β_2; the two cuts induce the same 'two-sidedness' locally.

Grothendieck then remarks: 'Je dis que cette condition est symétrique en les deux couples (A_i, β_i)', i.e. compatibility is a symmetric relation, an assertion left without proof.

The purpose is to build topological realizations of 'réseaux' (networks, graph-like combinatorial structures) by families of pairwise compatible cuts, i.e. non-crossing two-sided cuts. The dual combinatorics of such a family is a graph or network. This is in the spirit of Grothendieck's 1980s work on cartes, dessins and combinatorial surfaces.
errors: The symmetry of the compatibility relation is asserted ('Je dis que') but not proved. Since conditions (a)-(b) are phrased asymmetrically (cutting along A_1 first), symmetry is a genuine small claim. It is plausible for disjoint two-sided cuts, but it depends on the garbled condition (c) and on the hypothesis, noted in the NB on p.17, that A_i need not reduce to points.
Condition (c) as transcribed across pp.17-18 is incomplete, so the exact definition cannot be fully reconstructed.

ideas.what: Compatibility of two 'mesh structures' (cut locus with a choice of two banks) on a space: disjointness, plus the requirement that the induced two-sided bipartition is determined by both bank-pairs; claimed to be a symmetric relation
ideas.modern_name: Compatible / non-crossing two-sided cuts (disjoint separating or non-separating curves; compatible walls in a wallspace or pocset; tracks)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical in surface topology (curve systems, Dehn and Thurston); wallspaces and pocsets: Sageev 1995, Haglund-Paulin 1998; tracks: Dunwoody 1985
ideas.where_published: Related combinatorial-topological material on cartes and dessins appears in Esquisse d'un Programme (1984); this specific 'maille' formalism is not known to be published

deep.surprise_reason: This is a short closing fragment completing a fairly routine definition of compatible cuts ('mailles') and asserting that the relation is symmetric. It is foundational bookkeeping for realizing networks topologically, with no new result or unexpected connection beyond the generic resemblance to wallspace and curve-system formalisms.
transcription_corrections: 'alors {U,V} se définit : la [-fois-] réunion [?] ... B_1, et B_2' should read roughly 'alors {U,V} se définit à la fois [par] β_1 et β_2'. The symbols are β_1, β_2 (bank-pairs), not B_1, B_2, and 'réunion' is not supported; a crossed-out word precedes β_1.

'Je dis que cette condition, est un point symplectique sur les deux sommets (A_i, B_i)' should read 'Je dis que cette condition est symétrique en les deux couples (A_i, β_i)', with 'les deux' added above the line.
The '18' at the top is the page number, not an insertion.
